Note::remove_symbols¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::remove_symbols() const

Delete ASCII Punctuation And Control Bytes From Every Cell¶

remove_symbols() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, keeping only ASCII letters, ASCII digits, ASCII whitespace, and every non-ASCII byte. Everything else — ASCII punctuation (!, #, %, _, -, ., …) and ASCII control bytes (\t, \n, other C0 controls) — is deleted.

It is very close to remove_punctuation; the extra step is that remove_symbols also strips ASCII control characters. Both keep non-ASCII text intact, so accented and non-Latin words survive. If you want to drop non-ASCII too, use keep_alnum (which also drops whitespace) or keep_ascii first.

remove_symbols is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. Nothing is trimmed or collapsed.

Example 1: A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"100% (sure)!", "a_b-c", "café #9"}).remove_symbols())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["100 sure", "abc", "café 9"]

Example 2: Non-ASCII Text Is Kept¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note({"café — résumé"}).remove_symbols();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["café — résumé"]

The em dash and the accented letters are non-ASCII, so they stay; only ASCII punctuation/controls would have been removed.

See Also¶

  • Note::remove_punctuation: the same idea without also stripping ASCII control bytes.

  • Note::keep_alnum: keep only letters and digits (drops whitespace and non-ASCII).

  • Note::keep_printable: keep only visible ASCII.
